title: Draft a bodice block, move darts, and test it in a toile

say: Draft a bodice block, move darts, and test it in a toile.
This is the video for Module 2 of Advanced Tailoring and Pattern Making.
With the quarter method, you draft half the back and half the front. Each is a quarter of the body width.

panel.heading: Half the back, half the front
items: Each piece is one quarter of the body
Add a quarter of the ease to each
Formulas are starting points
The toile has the final word

say: So each piece gets a quarter of the ease. For example, Kemi has a 96 cm bust and a 78 cm waist. With 6 cm of bust ease and 4 cm at the waist, that is 1.5 cm and 1 cm per quarter.

say: Every formula is a starting point.

say: Your toile, not the formula, has the final word.

say: Draw the centre back line and mark the nape near the top. Measure down Kemi's nape to waist length, 39 cm, and square across for the waist.

panel.heading: Drafting the back bodice
items: Centre back line; nape to waist 39 cm
Armhole depth: 96 / 8 + 10 = 22 cm
Bust line: 24 + 1.5 = 25.5 cm
Neck, shoulder 12.5 cm, armhole curve
Waist 20.5 cm: 2 cm at side, 3 cm dart

say: Mark the armhole depth. A common starting value is bust divided by 8, plus 10 cm. For Kemi that is 22 cm. Square across. This is the bust line.

panel.heading: Drafting the back bodice
items: Centre back line; nape to waist 39 cm
Armhole depth: 96 / 8 + 10 = 22 cm
Bust line: 24 + 1.5 = 25.5 cm
Neck, shoulder 12.5 cm, armhole curve
Waist 20.5 cm: 2 cm at side, 3 cm dart

say: On the bust line, measure out a quarter of the bust plus ease. 24 plus 1.5 makes 25.5 cm. Square down for the side seam guide.

panel.heading: Drafting the back bodice
items: Centre back line; nape to waist 39 cm
Armhole depth: 96 / 8 + 10 = 22 cm
Bust line: 24 + 1.5 = 25.5 cm
Neck, shoulder 12.5 cm, armhole curve
Waist 20.5 cm: 2 cm at side, 3 cm dart

say: Draw the back neck curve and a sloping shoulder 12.5 cm long, then curve the armhole down to the side.

panel.heading: Drafting the back bodice
items: Centre back line; nape to waist 39 cm
Armhole depth: 96 / 8 + 10 = 22 cm
Bust line: 24 + 1.5 = 25.5 cm
Neck, shoulder 12.5 cm, armhole curve
Waist 20.5 cm: 2 cm at side, 3 cm dart

say: The waist quarter is 19.5 plus 1, which is 20.5 cm. The bust line is 25.5, so 5 cm must go. Take 2 cm at the side seam, and put 3 cm into a back waist dart.
The front is drafted the same way, with its bust point marked clearly.

panel.heading: Drafting the back bodice
items: Centre back line; nape to waist 39 cm
Armhole depth: 96 / 8 + 10 = 22 cm
Bust line: 24 + 1.5 = 25.5 cm
Neck, shoulder 12.5 cm, armhole curve
Waist 20.5 cm: 2 cm at side, 3 cm dart

say: Now compare the side seams. The back side seam is 39 minus 22, which is 17 cm.

panel.heading: Finding the side bust dart
items: Back side seam: 39 minus 22 = 17 cm
Front side seam: 20.5 cm, longer for the bust
Difference: 3.5 cm side bust dart
Fold it closed: front now 17 cm too

say: The front side seam is 20.5 cm. It is longer, because the front waist dropped lower to go over the bust.

panel.heading: Finding the side bust dart
items: Back side seam: 39 minus 22 = 17 cm
Front side seam: 20.5 cm, longer for the bust
Difference: 3.5 cm side bust dart
Fold it closed: front now 17 cm too

say: The side seams must be the same length to sew together. So the difference, 3.5 cm, becomes a side bust dart, pointing at the bust point and stopping 2.5 cm short of it.

panel.heading: Finding the side bust dart
items: Back side seam: 39 minus 22 = 17 cm
Front side seam: 20.5 cm, longer for the bust
Difference: 3.5 cm side bust dart
Fold it closed: front now 17 cm too

say: Fold the dart closed and measure again. The front side seam is now 17 cm, matching the back.

panel.heading: Finding the side bust dart
items: Back side seam: 39 minus 22 = 17 cm
Front side seam: 20.5 cm, longer for the bust
Difference: 3.5 cm side bust dart
Fold it closed: front now 17 cm too

say: Check your total too. 25.5 cm times 4 quarters is 102 cm, the body plus the ease.

panel.heading: Finding the side bust dart
items: Back side seam: 39 minus 22 = 17 cm
Front side seam: 20.5 cm, longer for the bust
Difference: 3.5 cm side bust dart
Fold it closed: front now 17 cm too
panel.rule: Seams that sew together must be the same length.

say: A dart is a wedge of fabric stitched away to shape flat cloth. On the front bodice, every dart points at the bust point.

panel.heading: Move the dart, keep the fit
items: Every front dart points at the bust point
Move it anywhere round the edge
Pivot, or slash and spread: same result
End it 2 to 3 cm short of the bust point
Both dart legs the same length

say: So you can move it anywhere around the edge, shoulder, neckline or waist. The fit stays the same. Only the look changes.

panel.heading: Move the dart, keep the fit
items: Every front dart points at the bust point
Move it anywhere round the edge
Pivot, or slash and spread: same result
End it 2 to 3 cm short of the bust point
Both dart legs the same length

say: Pivot the block on the bust point, or slash a paper copy and spread it. Both give the same result.

panel.heading: Move the dart, keep the fit
items: Every front dart points at the bust point
Move it anywhere round the edge
Pivot, or slash and spread: same result
End it 2 to 3 cm short of the bust point
Both dart legs the same length

say: Stop bust darts 2 to 3 cm short of the bust point, or you get a sharp peak.

panel.heading: Move the dart, keep the fit
items: Every front dart points at the bust point
Move it anywhere round the edge
Pivot, or slash and spread: same result
End it 2 to 3 cm short of the bust point
Both dart legs the same length

say: And keep both legs the same length, or the seam will not match.
For example, Halima in Kano moved a side dart to the shoulder, then turned it into a princess seam for an aso-ebi lace gown, with the same fit.

say: A toile is a test garment in cheap fabric, such as calico, of a similar weight to the final fabric.

panel.heading: Test the shape in cheap fabric
items: Cut in calico of similar weight
2 cm side seams so you can let them out
Mark bust, waist, hip, CF and CB lines
Sew with a long, easy-to-unpick stitch
Fit, pin and photograph with permission

say: Use 2 cm on the side seams, so you can let them out.

say: Drag lines, the diagonal wrinkles, point to where it is too tight. A gaping front neckline has too much length or width.

panel.heading: What the toile tells you
right: Add width at the side seam
Move a small wedge into the dart

say: Add width at the side seam on the bust line. Pin out the gape and move it into the bust dart. Shorten a sharp dart by 1 to 2 cm.
Then copy every correction onto the paper in a different colour, and move the tested block onto card.

panel.heading: What the toile tells you
right: Add width at the side seam
Move a small wedge into the dart

say: To remember. Draft in quarters. The side seam difference becomes the bust dart. Move darts around the bust point. And never cut the real fabric until the toile fits.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Quarter of the body plus quarter of the ease
Waist reduction: side seam plus a dart
Front minus back side seam = side bust dart
Darts move round the bust point
Correct the paper after every toile
